pulls.title: 8385995: C2: assert(phi->_idx >= nodes_size()) failed: only new Phi per instance memory slice
pulls.author: merykitty
pulls.body_excerpt: Hi, Before [JDK-8350971](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8350971), we only split a memory `Phi` when one of its outputs wants the slice corresponding to an alias class that is created by escape analysis. However, after the fix, we also split a memory `Phi` if one of its input needs splitting. This is problematic, because this also finds unrelated `Phi`s. And in one of those unrelated `Phi`s, we find a `Phi` that is created by an earlier iteration of EA. In `ConnectionGraph::find_inst_mem`, we try to look for a memory input if `alias_idx` corresponds to a `TypePtr` that `is_known_instance`.

pulls.author: shruacha1234
pulls.body_excerpt: When XSLT output method is html, characters supported by the target encoding were serialized as HTML entity references (for example, é as eacute;). This caused failures when the generated output was later processed as XML. **Solution:** Update HTML serializer to write characters directly when they are supported by the configured encoding, and retain existing entity escaping behavior for unsupported characters. **Testing:** Verified XSLT transformation with accented characters and confirmed generated output can be parsed successfully without XML parsing failures. pulls.title: 8386885: Parallel: Support dynamic young/old generation boundary
pulls.author: albertnetymk
pulls.body_excerpt: This change makes the Parallel GC generation boundary dynamic. The heap is still reserved as one contiguous range, with old gen at lower addresses and young gen at higher addresses, but the boundary between them can now move during GC. The current implementation fixes the old/young reserved split at startup. This limits how much reserved space each generation can use later. With a dynamic boundary, Parallel GC can transfer reserved space between old and young gen during GC. pulls.author: merykitty
pulls.body_excerpt: Hi, In principle, to hoist a store out of a loop, you need to peel the loop first, then move the store up past the entry of the first iteration. As a result, removing a store after peeling is a strictly more general transformation. Assume `p` and `p1` are independent, `p` and `v` are loop-invariants, we have: 0. loop (0..n) { Store(p1, v1); Store(p, v); StoreLoadFence(); } 1. Peel the first iteration Store(p1, v1); Store(p, v); StoreLoadFence(); loop (1..n) { Store(p1, v1); Store(p, v); StoreLoadFence(); } 2. pulls.title: 8378626: C2: Move LoadNodes above loops
pulls.author: merykitty
pulls.body_excerpt: Hi, Currently, a load can only be scheduled before a loop if all of its inputs are before that loop. In this PR, we try to hoist the load above a loop even when the memory input is not a loop-invariant. To do that, we try to analyze the loop, and if all memory accesses in the loop does not interfere with the load, we rewire the memory input of the load to the memory state at the loop entry. This allows the load to be scheduled before the loop. This transformation is performed during the early placement computation of the graph, right after we have built the `IdealLoopTree`.
